result.title: Large language models as oncology world models
result.comment: 63 pages (main text 35, Supplementary Information 28), 6 figures, 9 Extended Data figures. Code: https://github.com/julienvibert/llm-oncology-world-models. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24137512
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize cancer patient cases, but their internal representation of oncology, or world model, has not been explored systematically. By only specifying tumor type, we show that LLMs tend to generate similar patients per cancer, with on average 81.0% to 93.2% of a cancer's patients sharing the most frequent value of each baseline feature. By systematically varying patient features in 12 clinical scenarios, we show that they follow biomarker and treatment logic in 29 of 36 model-scenario assessments, against 1 of 12 when previous treatment or frailty matters. Continuing real patient trajectories, an LLM predicted 89.9% 12-month survival, and 79.2% with similar patients as examples, against 72.2% observed. To represent these trajectories, we developed the Clinical State Space, a dynamic representation framework that we also applied to real patients. Despite the limits we show, improved world models may support digital twins, which our framework can evaluate.

AI.brief_summary: 该文系统探测 LLM 内部的肿瘤学「世界模型」：仅给定肿瘤类型时生成的病例高度同质，在 12 个临床情境中多数只遵循生物标志物与治疗逻辑而在既往治疗或虚弱状态重要时失效，并提出 Clinical State Space 这一动态轨迹表示框架用于刻画真实与合成患者。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态空间」式轨迹表示与对状态随证据更新的检验思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的动态表示、信息保留与评价方式提供概念线索，但领域较远，可供核查。
